significance: One of the older Tamil shrines on the Penang mainland, set up in the 1870s by Indian labourers who came with the East India Company. It opened as Sri Muniandy Temple and was later renamed for Muniswarar, the village guardian deity worshipped at its main altar alongside Ganesha and Murugan.
story: The guardian is said to ride the neighbourhood after midnight on a white horse with an arivaal blade and a cigar, and a Chinese devotee who saw him enter the temple grounds so mounted paid for an altar in his honour.
